title: Exact Rank of Antler Functions
summary: The Antler-function rank is proved at most 2 to the power 10.43, while proving or correcting the experimentally suggested exact value 1088 remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the family of Antler functions $G_{S_1,S_2,S_3}$, let the rank be the dimension of the space spanned by all such functions. The proved upper bound is $2^{10.43}$, while experiments suggest that the rank is $1088=2^{10.09}$, without a theoretical explanation. Prove that the rank is exactly $1088$, or otherwise determine the exact rank and theoretically account for the experimentally observed value.

scope.domain: Structural rank analysis of the Antler family of Boolean functions.
parameters: S_1, S_2, S_3 — indices in the Antler function family
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that the rank is exactly 1088, or determine its exact value and theoretically explain the experimental observation.

progress.summary: The source proves a rank upper bound of 2 to the power 10.43, then reports experiments suggesting 1088. It explicitly states that this tighter value lacks a theoretical explanation.
citation_labels: Henri Gilbert et al., Cryptanalysis of Elisabeth-4
